Hi Ashley — thanks for the quick note and the attachments, those are super helpful. Sorry you hit the 502s during the POC. Quick responses up front, followed by a proposed M.A.P (mutual action plan):

Quick answers:
- SDK: v0.9.1 has a known batching change (improved throughput) but we shipped a patch in v0.9.3 that fixes a corner-case with large multipart payloads that can push request size past the gateway threshold. Recommend upgrading to 0.9.3 and re-running the failing batch.
- Timeouts/routing: defaults are conservative for latency; if your client batches many items into a single request the server-side decode + reranker scoring can push execution beyond the gateway timeout. Temporary mitigations: reduce batch_size to 8–12, or set request-level timeout to 90s.
- Immediate mitigation: switch to sequential smaller batches or set embed request header X-Redwood-Prefer=priority to route to lower-latency pool if available (we can enable that for your account).

Proposed M.A.P (next 48 hours):
1) You try v0.9.3 with batch_size=12 and share one failing request id (X-Request-ID header) if it still happens.
2) If it reproduces, we'll run a brief capture from our gateway for the specific request id and examine kernel-level timeouts and routing.
3) Karthik will join a short debugging call if you can reproduce; we can also enable a temporary canary with increased gateway timeout for your project.

Can you confirm availability for a 30-minute troubleshooting call today at 2pm PT? If that window doesn't work, we can do 4pm PT.

I'll cc Karthik for the engineering-side follow-up.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi all — Karthik from runtime/inference. Thanks for the detailed logs, Ashley — that made triage quick. A few notes from initial investigation: 

1) Cause hypothesis: large combined tokenization and reranker scoring window causing the request to exceed the gateway upstream_read_timeout. The sample_payload.json indicates you are sending structured-output metadata plus a 3-stage reranker (narrow -> broad -> final score) synchronously. That multiplies CPU + KV-cache pressure compared to a single pass.

2) Immediate mitigations to try now (short checklist):
- Upgrade SDK to redwood-js v0.9.3 (fixes oversized-multipart edge case).
- Reduce client batch_size to 8–12.
- Set request header X-Redwood-Client-Timeout=90000 (ms) for staging to test extended timeout.
- In reranker, change final scoring call to async (fire-and-forget / offload to a small background worker) while you validate results — we can help with pattern.

3) Workarounds we can enable from our side:
- Temporarily increase upstream timeout to 120s for your staging project (small transient risk to other tenants; requires approval).
- Enable a canary route that pins requests to a lower-latency GPU pool (good for short POC runs).

4) Next steps:
- If you can share one or two X-Request-ID values from the failing runs, I will pull the gateway logs and kernel timings and loop in infra.
- I've opened INF-2398 in our tracker to track the triage; I'll attach the gateway dump once we have IDs.

If you want, I can join the 2pm PT call to watch a repro. Otherwise I can take the logs and push a canary config for you to validate.
